en: So we saw 2 new algorithms in practice and
we also learned about cases.
Now, as I said, experience comes with
practice and therefore it is now time to
practice
what you learned and practice to work with
algorithms in general. Here's your task.
I want you to write 2 algorithms which will
actually work independent from each other.
The first algorithm should take an array of
numbers as input and return the minimum
value in the array, so the smallest number
you find in that array.
The second algorithm, which has nothing to
do with the first one,
should take a number as input, so not an
array, just a number,
and return true
if it's an even number or false if it's an
odd number.
Now besides those algorithms, those
functions. You should also define the time
complexities for those 2
algorithms, so find out what the time
complexities are, and also have a look at
possible cases you might have there.
That's your task. Definitely try it on your
own first. You need nothing more than what
you learned.
Then of course, definitely compare your
solution to mine, and of course also do so
if you're not able to come up with a
solution here No worries, there'll be plenty
of other opportunities to practice this in
this course.
